title: Bioelectric circuits act as software: multistable states switched without genetic change

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bioelectric circuits act as software: multistable states switched without genetic change

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Ion channel and gap junction circuits are well suited to the "software" of life because they form feedback loops that implement dynamical systems with multiple attractors, which transient signals can switch between without changing the hardware (i.e. without mutating the DNA encoding the channels).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: What makes electric circuits, whether ion channel-mediated or electronic, good for software is that they easily implement dynamical systems that have multiple attractors and can be made to occupy one physiological state or another by transient inputs (signals), not requiring changing the hardware (i.e., mutating the DNA encoding that hardware).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Discussion”. Scope: Bioelectric networks of ion channels and gap junctions in cells and tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-26: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Multistability and transient switching are standard dynamical properties testable with public models and software. The mechanistic core can be resolved now, although the software analogy itself is not empirical.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Construct or reuse ion-channel and gap-junction dynamical models, identify multiple stable physiological attractors, and demonstrate switching by transient inputs while parameters representing channel-encoding DNA remain fixed.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Existence in selected circuits does not show all bioelectric networks are multistable.

Software is a metaphor beyond the stated dynamical properties.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The computational content, multiple attractors switched by a transient input under fixed channel parameters, is what BETSE was built to explore and can be tested by a standard parameter sweep. That resolves the circuit claim inside the model. The biological reading, that tissues actually store anatomy this way, depends on experiments whose raw physiological traces are not deposited, and transcriptional storage remains a rival. Code makes the software analogy partly resolvable and leaves the tissue claim open.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In an ion-channel and gap-junction network, show at least two stable Vmem patterns and a transient stimulus that switches them with channel genes held fixed. Multistability under fixed parameters would support the software analogy in the model; a unique steady state, or a switch that requires changing channel expression, would refute it there. The tissue reading additionally needs a transient in vivo stimulus that permanently changes anatomy without a DNA change.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No public time series records an in vivo bioelectric switch and the subsequent attractor.

Transcriptional memory can store a new anatomical state with the DNA sequence unchanged.

A multistable model does not show that tissues occupy those attractors.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.5
data existence: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.7
